title: Till and Subsidy Accounting: Drawdown Order under the Workplace Cafe Management Program
content:
When an employee meal draws on client subsidy, the subsidy is calculated from the subsidy model printed against the service model in force: a percent discount model meets the stated percentage of the menu price, a fixed amount per meal model meets a flat amount per meal, a full model meets the whole menu price, and a model of none draws nothing at all.

Whatever the model yields is then held to the daily ceiling printed against the service model, measured as the total subsidy already drawn for that employee on that service day plus the subsidy this meal would draw; the excess above the ceiling is left with the employee to pay.

**Which lot is drawn.** Drawdowns are taken from funding lots in order of the day the lot was funded, oldest lot first, and a meal that exhausts one lot takes the remainder from the next lot in that order, producing one drawdown row per lot touched. A drawdown is only posted while the contract stands active, suspended or in transition out — this is read from the contract's own status on record, taken before the drawdown is posted, for that contract alone.

Where no drawable funding remains on the contract, no drawdown is posted: the employee pays the full menu price, and the shortfall is reported to the client on the next invoice rather than carried as a negative pool.

Every drawdown row carries the employee till transaction that caused it, so that a reversal of that till transaction can be matched back to the exact drawdown to be reversed. The subsidy model, the percentage of the menu price it meets, and the daily ceiling per employee are each those printed against the service model on the Workplace Cafe Management Program contract.
